newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX held back as Deutsche Telekom slips.
newsitem.headline: German DAX held back as Deutsche Telekom slips.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares, now including newly-floated Deutsche Telekom, ended floor trade on Tuesday only very slightly firmer as the new member lost some ground and weighed on the index.

Telekom shares, which traded for the first time on Monday in Europe's biggest initial public offering, ended bourse dealings down over five percent, or 1.83 marks at 32.07 marks, just higher than the day's low of 31.95 marks, but still well above the issue price of 28.50 marks.

Volumes in the market debutante were bigger than a normal day's trading in all the DAX 30 shares combined, with over 11 million changing hands in bourse dealings and almost fifteen million in computer trade.
Dealers said players were taking profit in the stock and were divided over whether Telekom would stablise around current levels or try to climb higher.
"Big and small investors are cashing in," said one trader.

Meanwhile, the DAX index, in which Telekom is now weighted at around 4.7 percent, ended down 0.25 points, or just 0.01 percent, at 2,764.09, after spending most of the session fluctuating around its Monday closing level.
Although most attention was still focused on Telekom, figures out at German haircare and cosmetics group Wella AG put the firm in the spotlight.

Preference shares in Wella tumbled nearly seven percent, dropping 59 marks to 810 marks, after the group announced a drop in group pre-tax profit for the first nine months of the year to 84.4 million marks from 88.1 million.
Wella preference shares hit a day's low of 791 marks, but recovered some ground after the company said it expected profits to rise 25 percent next year.

Meanwhile, shares in Germany's largest bank Deutsche Bank ended floor trade down 40 pfennigs at 71.10 marks as they caught up with losses made in in very thin late Monday computer dealing sparked by just one order, dealers said.
